newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala grants nine oil exploration concessions.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala grants nine oil exploration concessions.

text.p: Guatemala's Energy and Mines Ministry has granted nine concessions for oil exploration to five different companies, an official said Tuesday.

Canadian company Rank Resources Inc won a seismic option contract and an exploitation contract and Oil Technology Services of the United States was granted a production sharing contract, energy ministry spokesman Henry Hernandez told Reuters.

Hernandez said the government also granted a Guatemalan firm, Compania Petrolera de Atlantico, one seismic option contract and a production sharing contract. Argentina's Compania General de Combustibles also received concessions.
Basic Resources International Ltd, Guatemala's sole oil producer, also received two contracts, one for seismic option and one for exploitation.
The call for bids on 12 sites for petroleum and natural gas exploration and exploitation went out in January.
Basic produces 23,000 barrels of crude oil a day from 14 wells. The low-grade petroleum is all exported.
For two days last week production was halted at Basic's mini-refinery in the Peten department of northern Guatemala when hundreds of disgruntled former civil defense patrollers occupied the site.
But after a brief standoff with the army and the police the protestors, who were demanding payment for wartime service, agreed to abandon their protest.
Despite the recent disturbance in the Peten, Energy Minister Leonel Lopez told reporters interest in oil exploration has increased since the December conclusion of Guatemala's 36-year civil war.
The ministry anticipates that total investment in petroleum exploration and production, including the new concessions and 14 previous contracts, will reach $127 million in 1998.
The ministry projects Guatemala's oil production will reach 40,000 barrels a day by December 1998.
Many of the areas to be explored are in remote, jungle- covered parts of Guatemala's Peten department.
Oil companies will be able to construct pipelines along the same rights-of-way used by Basic, which has constructed pipelines to the seven fields where it produces oil here.
